title: Acids, Bases, and Salts - Chemistry - Definitions (Arrhenius & Brønsted–Lowry)
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: According to the Arrhenius definition, what does an acid produce when dissolved in water?
questions.explain: An Arrhenius acid is a substance that increases the concentration of hydrogen ions ($H^+$) when dissolved in water.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the Brønsted–Lowry theory, a base is defined as a substance that:
questions.explain: The Brønsted–Lowry theory defines a base as a proton ($H^+$) acceptor.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Identify the conjugate base of sulfuric acid ($H_2SO_4$).
questions.explain: A conjugate base is formed when an acid loses one proton. $H_2SO_4 \rightarrow H^+ + HSO_4^-$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the conjugate acid of ammonia ($NH_3$)?
questions.explain: A conjugate acid is formed when a base accepts a proton. $NH_3 + H^+ \rightarrow NH_4^+$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q:
Consider the following equilibrium reaction:
$$CH_3COOH(aq) + H_2O(l) \rightleftharpoons CH_3COO^-(aq) + H_3O^+(aq)$$
Which species acts as the Brønsted–Lowry base in the forward reaction?
questions.explain: In the forward reaction, $H_2O$ accepts a proton from acetic acid ($CH_3COOH$) to become $H_3O^+$, making it the base.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following substances is amphoteric (can act as both an acid and a base)?
questions.explain: Water ($H_2O$) is amphoteric because it can donate a proton to become $OH^-$ or accept a proton to become $H_3O^+$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
